How many additional eligible contact hours are needed for that calendar year? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: 6 contact hours
3 contact hours
4 contact hours
12 contact hours

choices.text: 6 contact hours
14 contact hours

Required vaccine training, documented on-the-job assessment, and current CPR are not all complete. What must be addressed before this staff member vaccinates under the state policy? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The described personnel qualifications are satisfied.
Complete or restore the stated training/CPR requirements first.
Obtain full technician licensure; trainee status is not sufficient.
Complete the certification-or-post-licensure-experience pathway first.

visible_originals.stem:
A pharmacy could not supply the full quantity of 60 units on a CII prescription and dispensed 20. Exactly 72 hours have elapsed since that shortage partial. The remaining stock is now available; no patient-request or LTCF exception was used, and all other dates remain valid.

Which action follows the stock-shortage partial-fill rule? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Dispense a new full quantity of 60 units because the prescription is still in date.
Complete up to the remaining 40 units under the original shortage-partial route.
Start a new 72-hour period when replacement stock arrives.
Notify the prescriber; later supply requires a new prescription.

visible_originals.stem:
A Massachusetts pharmacist reviews buprenorphine specifically for opioid use disorder. The prescriber has authorized at least 90 days, the prescription is otherwise in date, and no separate patient-specific or product limit is more restrictive. Evaluate the statutory single-fill ceiling, not whether the pharmacy should supply that entire amount.

Under Policy 2024-05 and c.94C §23(d), what is the applicable maximum days-supply category? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: 7 days
90 days
30 days
60 days

Case A: A reportable unsecured-PHI breach affects exactly 500 individuals, all residing in one state; no other media-notice trigger is present.

Case B: A separate breach affects 501 residents of one state.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The first breach meets the 500-or-more threshold for the specified HHS reporting route.
A required media notice replaces the individual notices.
The second breach fails the media threshold because 501 is not more than 500.
The first breach meets the more-than-500 media threshold solely because exactly 500 residents are affected.

visible_originals.stem:
Case A: An uncollected prescription has never left the pharmacy's control, and staff propose pouring the tablets back into the manufacturer's stock bottle.

Case B: Instead, staff consider keeping an eligible return-to-stock supply in its patient container or another appropriate labeled container.

Which statements accurately apply to the described cases or the related requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: Uncollected tablets may be poured into the manufacturer's bottle because the patient never received them.
A prepared but uncollected prescription differs from medicine already dispensed to a patient.
A new RTS container permits removal of product identification and assignment of a fresh expiration.
An occasional RTS transaction is exempt from the described written procedure requirement.

visible_originals.stem:
Case A: A patient wants a Schedule II medicine quickly, but appropriate alternative treatment is available and a lawful written prescription can reasonably be supplied before dispensing.

Case B: Another case involves an electronic-system outage, and staff assume the outage alone satisfies every federal emergency-oral criterion.

Which statements accurately apply to the described cases or the related requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: An electronic outage does not by itself establish every oral-emergency condition.
Convenience does not meet the combined federal emergency criteria described in the notes.
Every qualifying oral Schedule II emergency authorizes a fixed seven-day quantity.
An oral emergency converts Schedule II into a refillable prescription.

Case A: For an eligible protected-care Schedule VI prescription, the prescriber requests the permitted practice-name label treatment.

Case B: Staff apply the same Schedule VI exception to testosterone and delete the actual prescriber identity from the pharmacy's original record.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Using a practice name means prescriber-identity verification is no longer necessary.
The eligible Schedule VI request must be assessed under the specific practice-name label pathway.
The Schedule VI label exception authorizes both the testosterone label change and erasure of internal prescriber identity.
Use in gender-affirming care makes every medicine Schedule VI.

visible_originals.stem:
Case A: A medicine's current labeling requires a condition outside the pharmacy's general refrigerator or freezer ranges, but staff use the general range without checking the product.

Case B: A pharmacy stores medication in a dorm-style refrigerator with a small freezer compartment inside the refrigerator and also keeps staff meals there.

Which statements accurately apply to the described cases or the related requirements? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: A closed refrigerator door alone proves suitable medication storage.
Unopened manufacturer expiration applies unchanged after every reconstitution or opening.
The actual product's approved storage and stability requirements must be considered rather than replaced by a general range.
A dorm-style unit containing staff meals is compliant whenever it feels cold.

visible_originals.stem: On Friday morning, a pharmacy discovers a significant unexplained loss of controlled substances. The investigation cannot be completed that day. Which federal response is correct?

choices.text: Wait for the investigation before contacting DEA.
Give oral notice within 24 hours and take no further action.
File Form 106 within one business day instead of separate notice.
Send written DEA notice within one business day and Form 106 within 45 calendar days.
Notify only the Massachusetts Board because the loss occurred in Massachusetts.

visible_originals.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is preparing for renewal. In the first calendar year of the two-year renewal cycle, she completed 24 contact hours. In the second calendar year, she has completed 16 contact hours. Her pharmacy-law and home-study requirements are otherwise satisfied. What is the best way to address the remaining CE requirement?

choices.text: Renew now because the Board looks only at the combined 40-hour total for the two-year cycle.
Complete 4 more contact hours in the second calendar year because the 20-hour minimum applies to each calendar year.
Complete only additional pharmacy-law hours; the annual total no longer matters once the law requirement is met.
Ask the CE provider to redate 4 first-year credits so they count in the second calendar year.
Repeat all 20 second-year hours because completing more than 20 hours in the first year invalidates the surplus-year record.

visible_originals.stem: A patient returns an unopened bottle that a Massachusetts pharmacy dispensed in error. The product appears intact. Which actions are required or permitted for the returned medication? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Accept the return because it was previously dispensed in error by the pharmacy.
Do not place the returned medication back into dispensing inventory merely because the container is unopened.
Segregate or quarantine the returned medication and handle its disposition under the pharmacy's required return/disposal process.
Keep the returned medication out of active dispensing inventory while it awaits proper disposition.
Dispense the returned bottle to another patient after a pharmacist visually inspects the seal.

visible_originals.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy receives a valid oxycodone Schedule II prescription for 30 tablets but has only 12 tablets in stock. The patient wants the full prescribed quantity; the pharmacy dispenses 12 solely because it cannot supply the rest. Four days later the remaining stock arrives. What is the controlling federal consequence?

choices.text: The balance may be dispensed within 30 days because every Schedule II partial fill uses the patient-requested 30-day pathway.
The pharmacy may treat the remaining 18 tablets as a refill because the original total quantity was not dispensed.
The remaining 18 tablets may be transferred to another pharmacy once the original pharmacy receives stock.
The ordinary 72-hour shortage-remainder period has passed, so further quantity generally requires prescriber notification and a new prescription.
The original pharmacy may dispense the balance at any time before the Massachusetts 30-day Schedule II validity period ends.

visible_originals.stem: A properly authorized New Hampshire practitioner telephones a lawful alprazolam prescription to a Massachusetts pharmacist. The pharmacist verifies the Schedule IV prescription under the out-of-state pathway. A staff member says the pharmacy must wait for a written prescription before dispensing. Which response is most accurate?

choices.text: Treat the call as a Schedule II emergency prescription and require the Schedule II follow-up process before any dispensing.
Use the Schedule III-V oral pathway; record a request for the practitioner's written prescription within seven days or any shorter controlling federal period.
Dispense now and wait six months before asking the practitioner for any written record.
Ask the patient to create and sign the written follow-up because the original prescription was oral.
Reject every out-of-state oral Schedule III-V prescription because Massachusetts recognizes only electronic out-of-state prescriptions.

visible_originals.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist has completed the required administration training and maintains current CPR certification. Each option involves a medication that appears on the MH/SUD administration list. Which requests may proceed under the current guidance? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A 34-year-old patient has a valid patient-specific prescription for a repeat dose of Vivitrol supplied in its single-dose presentation
A 45-year-old patient has a valid patient-specific prescription for Invega Sustenna, but this would be the patient's first dose of the medication
A 39-year-old patient requests Abilify Maintena from anonymous pharmacy floor stock that is not tied to a patient-specific prescribed single dose
A 17-year-old patient has a valid patient-specific prescription for a repeat dose of Invega Sustenna
A 52-year-old patient has a valid patient-specific prescription for a repeat dose of Abilify Maintena supplied as the prescribed single dose

visible_originals.stem: Which statements correctly distinguish common federal OUD medication pathways? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Buprenorphine-naloxone remains Schedule III; the naloxone component does not make the product noncontrolled
Methadone for ongoing OUD maintenance is not handled as an ordinary community-pharmacy Schedule II pain prescription outside the applicable narcotic-treatment framework
Methadone and buprenorphine are legally interchangeable simply because both can treat OUD
Buprenorphine becomes Schedule VI in Massachusetts when used for OUD
A qualifying buprenorphine Schedule III prescription for OUD can use the ordinary prescription-dispensing framework when all current prescribing requirements are met

visible_originals.stem: A prescriber's office telephones a Massachusetts pharmacy with a new prescription while the pharmacist on duty is counselling another patient. Which statements about who may take the call are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Only the pharmacist may take a new prescription by telephone.
Any pharmacy employee may take it and pass it to the pharmacist to check.
A pharmacy intern may receive a new prescription over the telephone.
An uncertified technician may take it provided the pharmacist verifies it afterwards.
A certified technician with the on-duty pharmacist's approval may receive it.

visible_originals.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is filling a written prescription for a controlled substance dispensed as capsules. Which items must appear on the label the pharmacist affixes to the container? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The prescribing practitioner's registration number.
The filling pharmacist's initials.
The serial number of the prescription.
The number of capsules in the container.
The date of filling, and the pharmacy name and address.

visible_originals.stem:
A pharmacist has 13 eligible hours and finishes a 9-hour conference on a single day. Live, law, and specialized-topic requirements are satisfied.

How many conference hours may be applied under the stated daily CE limit? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: 8 conference hours.
7 conference hours.
9 conference hours.
6 conference hours.

visible_originals.stem:
A technician's Massachusetts license remains active, but national certification expired yesterday. A new Schedule IV prescription is telephoned to the pharmacy.

Who should receive this new prescription under the personnel distinctions in the notes? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Route this new Schedule IV order to a recipient whose current scope permits it.
This technician, provided the call is described as a refill in the computer.
This technician, provided the pharmacist signs the entry before dispensing.
A trainee, provided the caller repeats the prescription to two employees.

visible_originals.stem:
A fully licensed technician has worked 520 hours after full licensure, has current CPR, and has completed the required six-hour vaccine course. National certification is not held. The documented on-the-job skills training has not yet occurred.

Which remaining requirement is identified by these facts? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Repeating 500 hours as a trainee before using the completed full-license hours.
Obtaining national certification because experience cannot be used instead.
Completing a PharmD before any supervised vaccine administration.
The additional documented on-the-job training and skills checklist.

visible_originals.stem:
A practitioner issues several Schedule II prescriptions during one visit and wants the second prescription used later.

How should the issuance date and delayed-use instruction be represented under the federal multiple-prescription framework? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Use the intended pickup date as the issuance date on the second prescription.
Use the previous prescription's last-fill date as the new issuance date.
Use the actual issuance date and a separate earliest-fill instruction.
Leave the issuance date blank for the pharmacist to complete at pickup.

visible_originals.stem:
A pharmacy dispenses 12 tablets from a valid prescription for 30 oxycodone tablets solely because of stock shortage. No patient- or prescriber-requested partial-fill pathway was established. More than 72 hours after that partial fill, the rest becomes available.

What is required before supplying additional tablets under these facts? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Reclassify the original shortage as a patient request without further documentation.
Notify the prescriber and obtain a new prescription for further supply.
Transfer the remaining 18 tablets as an unused initial EPCS prescription.
Dispense the remainder because the prescription is less than 30 days old.

visible_originals.stem:
A Schedule II prescription is faxed for a resident of a qualifying long-term-care facility. The pharmacy has verified the required prescriber and patient information; other applicable requirements are satisfied.

What is the federal effect of the LTCF fax exception? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: The fax is valid only as a follow-up to a previous emergency dispensing.
The fax permits release only if an emergency oral order is also obtained.
Treat this qualifying LTCF fax as the original, subject to the other requirements.
The fax permits preparation, but a paper original is required before release.

visible_originals.stem:
A valid Schedule III prescription authorizes 60 tablets for the current fill. At the patient's request, the pharmacy dispenses 20 and later 25 tablets. The issue-date time limit has not expired.

What is the maximum quantity remaining under that 60-tablet authorization? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: 20 tablets.
60 tablets.
15 tablets.
35 tablets.

visible_originals.stem:
A reconstituted product has a short labeled in-use period. Its unopened manufacturer's expiration is months away, and the patient's prescription remains valid for the rest of the year.

Which conclusion follows? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Limit use of the prepared product to its applicable in-use period.
Refrigerating the product restarts its manufacturer's expiration.
The prescription's annual validity becomes the prepared product's BUD.
A refill authorization permits use after the product's in-use limit.

visible_originals.stem:
A Massachusetts pharmacist reviews four otherwise valid II–III prescriptions. Each requests an appropriate quantity within other applicable limits.

Which categories are included in the stated single-fill 90-day allowance? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: The qualifying implantable-infusion-pump category.
An ordinary Schedule II opioid pain prescription solely because the patient has used it before.
A non-opioid Schedule II medication.
Buprenorphine prescribed for opioid use disorder.
Every Schedule III product regardless of treatment purpose or category.

visible_originals.stem:
A pharmacy discovers a confirmed controlled-substance theft. Its investigation will take several weeks. The manager proposes making no written contact with DEA until the completed electronic Form 106 is ready.

Which timeline correctly separates the two federal duties? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Notice: 45 days after discovery; Form 106: 1 business day after notice.
Notice: 1 business day; completed Form 106: 45 days after discovery.
Notice: 1 business day; completed Form 106: 45 days after investigation ends.
Notice and completed Form 106: both 45 days after discovery.

visible_originals.stem:
A hospital's medical staff executive committee approved a pharmacist's CDTM service. The same physician-pharmacist team now plans to provide CDTM inside a separately licensed long-term care facility. The team's agreement and individual qualifications are otherwise suitable, but no approval has been obtained from that facility's medical director or designee.

Which action is needed for the new setting? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Obtain approval from the long-term care facility's medical director or designee.
File the hospital committee's approval as a substitute for the facility approval.
Use the retail CDTM pathway because the pharmacist also works at a community pharmacy.
Ask the dispensing pharmacy's MOR to approve the service in place of the medical director.

visible_originals.stem:
A prescriber telephones a new Schedule VI prescription. The pharmacist on duty approves a Massachusetts-licensed technician with current national certification to receive the call. The prescriber supplies the drug, strength, directions, quantity, and other required information. No therapeutic clarification is needed.

Which workflow is consistent with the technician’s scope? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Route the call to the pharmacist because technician telephone authority is limited to unchanged refills.
Have the technician identify as certified and receive the order for pharmacist review.
Have the technician receive the order and complete its final dispensing verification.
Have the technician complete the clinical review because the prescriber supplied every required field.

visible_originals.stem:
The sole pharmacist at a pharmacy that does not provide vaccination services is a registered pharmacist preceptor. Three technicians are scheduled to prepare prescriptions. One has just learned that national certification expired the previous day; all three Massachusetts technician licenses remain active. The other two technicians have no national certification.

Which staffing change permits a three-person filling team to work under the ordinary ratio? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: Retain the team after changing the lapsed employee's badge from certified technician to pharmacy technician.
Substitute a Massachusetts-licensed intern, under the pharmacist's direct supervision, for one of the technicians.
Retain the team while the lapsed employee's recertification application is pending with the certifying organization.
Substitute a state-licensed technician trainee for the lapsed employee and have the trainee work under direct supervision.
